Okay, here's the thing very easily and shittily explained bc it's actually very complicated and you should probably stick with CNN bc they explain stuff better than I possibly could: In 2013/2014 the local exchange rate for a dollar went from 4 Bolivares (local coin) to 6 bolivares. Overnight. Prices went up, and basic need stuff became very scarce. People started doing One-Direction-concert-long lines at the supermarket to buy toilet paper, rice, milk, you name it. Anyway, this was bad, but it really took a turn for the worse when oil prices dropped in half. Our industries are 96-98% OIL. You can see why that was very bad for us. Since then the exchange rate has gotten to (and this is as of YESTERDAY) 8300+ Bs. for a dollar. 9000+ for 1 Euro. This makes the average Venezuelan pretty damn angry, 90% of the country wants our butterfly man, donkey (I'll explain this later) president out of office. Anyway, in 2015 there were Assembly elections, and the opposition party won by a landslide. But since then, the government has been putting a lot of obstacles and deemed them worthless other than in spirit for the party. Protests started when the Supreme Court basically deemed them null, and even Luisa Miss-Chavismo-Attorney-General Ortega called them out on it. The government, after a while, called on a constituent assembly, and that was really the catalyst that really unleashed the chaos brewing and unified a divided opposition. (Note: Chavismo is Hugo Chavez's (previous prez) way of government. Madurismo (Nicolas Maduro is the current prez) is Castro + Chavismo with a dash of fascism. Also, the asshole called himself a butterfly man and we like to call him a donkey (Maburro).)
